walls.note: The SW flank (ring edge 2, 12.7 m). The brief's crop (TMX7316010203-001643_pano_0002_000113, 2020, 28 deg off) and six more views along the Damrak from the south (TMX7316010203-001643_pano_0002_000115/000116/000289, -001658_pano_0000_002044/002045, -002623_pano_0003_000053; 2020-2022) all show the flank behind the Damrak 38-41 row (Hotel Continental, Mannekenpis, Delta Hotel): what the crop's right third shows is the SE front at a grazing angle. Above the neighbours' cornices only a plain strip of the stone flank and the corner pinnacle (listed on the front) show; nothing notable. The flank is drawn as the 3DBAG shell in the front's stone.

items.where: stone dormer gable over the SW bay (x 45-200, cornice to y 30: h 17.4-21.7): vertical cheeks to shoulders at h 20.1, concave curves in to a neck (x 97-150), a moulded cap; a round-arched two-light window with a curved transom bar in a stone ring (x 80-165, y 150-245)
the NE bay's dormer in the slate mansard (x 270-335, window y 185-245) under a tall pointed slate spire with a ball finial (tip y 50, h 21.3)
small slate cone with a ball finial on a square stone base on the SW corner over the cornice (x 0-45, y 120-250, h 17.3-19.9)
slate mansard between the gable and the NE corner, cornice to y 120 (h 19.9), its sheer 3DBAG wall behind
items.how: a slate skin leaning from 0.45 m out at the cornice crown back to the shell wall top (muntplein-1 mansardSkin)

items.where: the shop window of the SW bay: one wide segmental-arched opening (x 35-205, y 880-1075, h 0.9-4.8) with two mullions and a waved Art Nouveau glazing bar at the springing, a moulded stone archivolt (to y 855), three basement lights below (y 1080-1105)

the entrance in the NE bay: a segmental-arched doorway (x 255-345, y 875-1075) in a stone surround, a glazed fanlight, the dark door recessed, three stone steps; two corbels (x 230-245, 380-395, y 840-870) carry the projecting bay above
third storey of the SW bay: three round-arched windows (x 35-80, 100-148, 165-210; y 318-430, h 13.8-16.0) under linked stone archivolts
third storey of the NE bay: a wide round-arched three-light window (x 262-345, y 318-385) in a large stone ring (top y 300)
the stone parapet panel of the NE bay under the arched window (x 240-375, y 385-440, h 13.5-14.6), carved with two round reliefs (masks or rosettes, centres x 270 and 330, about 0.6 m across)
items.how: a projecting stone panel with two raised discs in rings, each with a smaller boss: the carving's figures are not drawn

moulded stone cornice on brackets across the front at y 245-262 (h 17.1-17.4), string course at y 840-850 over the ground storey

walls.note: The Damrak front (ring edge 3, 8.57 m, t from the SW corner), read on the rectified 2025 crop w02-131.jpg (50.2 px/m, warm dusk light) and the overcast 2018 crop w02-131.alt.jpg (same layout). Heights h = (1120 - y) / 50.2 from the pavement: the gable cap lands at 21.7 m (3DBAG roof max 21.4), the cornice crown at 17.4 m (3DBAG SW corner wall 17.8). The facade spans x 0-400 of the 422 px crop (8.0 of 8.4 m); t = x / 50.2 + 0.25 centres it on the 8.57 m ring edge. Two bays: the wider SW bay (x 0-230) under the stone gable, the NE bay (x 230-395) a shallow projecting bay on two consoles over the entrance, under the slate mansard and its spired dormer.

budget: hand triangles about 6-9k: gable and spires 1k, 15 windows with surrounds 3k, arches and archivolts 2k, cornice and brackets 0.6k, reliefs 0.4k
